body.cap: Phantomics received the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the digital healthcare sector for its non-invasive myocardial disease diagnostic solution ‘Myomics.’ │Photo by AVING News

body.x: Biotech startup Phantomics participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time), to showcase its medical AI solution ‘Myomics.’

Phantomics possesses image biomarker technology that provides rapid and accurate diagnostic results through medical images such as MRI or CT. Based on this technology, the company introduced the myocardial disease diagnostic solution ‘Myomics.’ Phantomics continues its research and development to expand the scope of non-invasive diagnostic solutions for rapid and accurate diagnoses in cardiovascular, liver, and muscle wasting diseases.

Biopsy tests of myocardial tissues by inserting a catheter into the heart were essential for accurately diagnosing and monitoring many heart diseases. The company explains the Myomics-virtual biopsy as a safe, fast, and accurate non-invasive AI diagnostic solution replacing invasive myocardial tissue tests.

Non-invasive diagnostics, such as Phantomics’ Myomics, diagnose without creating holes or incisions in the body. Representative non-invasive diagnostic technologies include X-rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and computed tomography (CT). While non-invasive diagnostics are less painful and more comfortable than invasive methods that require creating wounds in the body, they are known to have lower accuracy. However, recent technological advancements have improved the range and accuracy of non-invasive diagnostics. Phantomics released Myomics in early 2022, using cardiac MRI to extract dozens of image biomarkers non-invasively. This allows for the safe and accurate diagnosis of myocardial diseases such as heart failure, myocarditis, and amyloidosis.

Regarding this solution, a Phantomics representative stated, “We have developed the optimal model using the best artificial intelligence algorithms, and we have optimized it based on local data to enhance diagnostic accuracy. We have also implemented a sophisticated algorithm that allows continuous updates for all publicly available clinical evidence up to the present.”

body.cap: Reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus is interviewing at the Phantomics booth. │Photo by AVING News

body.x: Recognizing such technological capabilities, Phantomics received the Innovation Award in the digital healthcare sector at CES 2024.

In addition, Myomics was praised for its optimized explanation function for doctors, nurses, patients, and caregivers and its workflow that approaches the presentation of essential evidence, available in all systems such as hospital information systems, web, and mobile.

The representative stated, “Currently, Myomics is used in major hospitals in Korea, Japan, China, Taiwan, and Singapore. We have obtained approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. We have also completed sales contracts with medical device distributors in Southeast Asia and South America and are in the process of obtaining local medical device approvals.” He added, “We participated in CES to introduce our differentiated products to medical companies in North America and Europe. By revolutionizing MRI interpretation, we aim to provide rapid and accurate information to doctors, contributing to human health.”

body.x: CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
